Article XI §11.5 strengthening of pkg/capture's TestListDisplays /
TestListWindows / TestParseXdotoolGeometry caught three real
defects that the previous bluff tests masked:

1. listLinuxDisplays fabricated a "Default Display" with 0x0
   dimensions when no xrandr / no $DISPLAY was available. Code
   downstream that consumed this fake display would later fail in
   confusing ways with no diagnostic. Now returns a typed
   errNoDisplayBackend that callers SKIP on.

2. listLinuxWindows returned (nil, nil) when neither xdotool nor
   wmctrl was installed — same fake-success pattern. Now returns
   a typed errNoWindowListTool.

3. parseXdotoolGeometry was broken by xdotool's two-space leading
   indentation: strings.Split on " " produced empty leading
   tokens, so Position/Geometry values never landed in the Window
   struct. The "test" only logged the always-zero result. Now uses
   strings.Fields and a proper switch on the keyword token.

The strengthened tests SKIP honestly with explicit
SKIP-OK: #CAPTURE-NO-DISPLAY / #CAPTURE-NO-WMCTRL markers when
the host lacks the required tools, so absence-of-coverage is
loud, not silent.

bluff-scan companion changes:
- ADBExecutor.Type() and 16 lifecycle tests already annotated in

- This commit annotates 8 capture-package smoke tests with

  Darwin-only tests).

Phase 2 Step 2.9 — PELT (Killick, Fearnhead & Eckley 2012) lands as
pure-Go, avoiding the Kickoff-brief ruptures Python sidecar. Same
decision pattern as SSIM: for ≤ thousands of samples the pure-Go DP
is sub-millisecond and Go stays CGO-free + sidecar-free.

pkg/analysis/pelt/pelt.go:
- PELT struct with MinSize (default 2) + pluggable Cost func.
- Segment(ctx, series, penalty) returns change-point indices —
  strictly increasing, within (0, n), after the first (implicit)
  segment boundary.
- Pruning step (Killick 2012 §3): at each tau, drop candidates whose
  F[s] + cost(s, tau) already exceeds F[tau] — those can never be
  optimal for any future tau'. Expected O(n) post-pruning.
- Exported CostFunc type so callers can plug in variance-change,
  rbf-kernel, or likelihood-based costs without touching the DP
  machinery.
- gaussianMeanCost: sum of squared deviations from segment mean
  (default, matches ruptures L2 cost).
- VarianceCost: -log σ² scaled by segment length — exported for
  scale-shift detection (mean-constant, variance-changing).
- Respects ctx.Err() every 256 tau steps.
- Sentinel errors: ErrEmptySeries, ErrNegativePenalty, ErrInvalidMinSize.

pkg/analysis/pelt/pelt_test.go (20 tests):
- Happy path: step change detected within ±5 of the true split,
  three-segment signal yields ≥ 2 CPs, constant → 0 CPs, higher
  penalty ⇒ fewer-or-equal CPs (BIC monotonicity).
- Return-shape invariants: strictly increasing, in (0, n).
- Config: MinSize=10 enforced, custom CostFunc (zero-cost → 0 CPs),
  VarianceCost catches scale shift that mean cost misses.
- Cost-function math: gaussianMeanCost zero/positive/empty,
  VarianceCost penalises variance / too-short / zero-variance floor.
- Error paths: nil/empty series, negative penalty, invalid MinSize,
  too-short series (no error, empty CPs), canceled ctx.
- Segmenter interface conformance (runtime + compile-time).

Coverage: 100% of statements. Race-clean.

Article VII 4-artefact rule — this milestone adds all four:
- unit + math tests (pelt_test.go, 20 cases).
- banks/phase2-gocore.yaml — PH2-PELT-001/002/003/004 (bank now 34
  total cases).
- challenges/config/helixqa-validation.yaml — HQA-PHASE2-GOCORE-008.
- banks/fixes-validation.yaml — FIX-OC4-008 pruning + monotonicity
  regression guard (guards against the pruning step silently losing
  optimality or producing non-monotone BIC behaviour).

Phase 2 Step 2.9 per OpenClawing4-Phase2-Kickoff.md §3 CLOSED without
needing the ruptures Python sidecar.

Phase 2 steps remaining:
- Step 2.6 (CDP web AX) — still blocked on vendoring go-rod.
- Step 2.10 (EI wire client) — Phase 1 tail, substantial work.

Everything else in Phase 2's original plan is shipping or code-complete.

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="Phase 24.0: stream multipart body in pkg/audio HTTP clients

Constitution §11.4 / Phase 23.8+23.9 follow-up. Memory-safety fix.

The Phase 23.8+23.9 Whisper/Tesseract clients buffered the entire
input file into a bytes.Buffer before sending. For QA video clips
(typically 10–100 MB) this is fine; for a 2-hour 1080p capture
(~10 GB) it would OOM the test runner. Phase 24.0 replaces the
in-memory pattern with an io.Pipe streaming helper so only ~64 KiB
sits in RAM at any instant.

New: pkg/audio/stream.go — streamSingleFileMultipart(partName, path)
returns an io.Reader backed by io.Pipe. A goroutine writes the
multipart-encoded file into the pipe writer; the http client reads
from the reader. Open failure surfaces synchronously (no goroutine
spawned). Goroutine-leak-safe: PipeWriter.Close on early-close
unblocks io.Copy with ErrClosedPipe; goroutine exits via deferred
close. File handle closed in the goroutine.

Refactored:
  whisper_client.go   — Transcribe uses streamSingleFileMultipart
  tesseract_client.go — OCR + OCRVideo use streamSingleFileMultipart
                       — old buildSingleFileMultipart deleted

New tests (3 cases, all PASS):
  TestStream_OpenFailureSynchronous          — early failure surfaces
  TestStream_LargeFileEndToEnd_ByteIdentical — 5 MiB random payload
                                                round-trips with
                                                SHA256 match (asserts
                                                streaming actually
                                                preserves all bytes)
  TestStream_NoGoroutineLeakOnEarlyClose      — 5 partial-receive
                                                iterations, goroutine
                                                count stable

Article XI §11.5 strengthening of pkg/capture's TestListDisplays /

   downstream that consumed this fake display would later fail in

   indentation: strings.Split on " " produced empty leading
   tokens, so Position/Geometry values never landed in the Window
   struct. The "test" only logged the always-zero result. Now uses
   strings.Fields and a proper switch on the keyword token.

SKIP-OK: #CAPTURE-NO-DISPLAY / #CAPTURE-NO-WMCTRL markers when

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(gpu/infer): reusable Triton KServe v2 client (M53)

Phase 4 foundation. Every future GPU sidecar HelixQA talks to
— qa-vision-infer, qa-video-decode, qa-vulkan-compute,
UI-TARS-via-Triton, OmniParser-via-Triton — speaks the same wire.
This package factors the common KServe v2 inference wire code
into one reusable Client so downstream model-specific clients
become thin wrappers.

pkg/gpu/infer/infer.go:
- Client with Endpoint, HTTPClient, InferPath.
- Request { Model, Inputs[] }; Input supports every Triton
  datatype (BYTES / FP32 / FP64 / INT32 / INT64 / UINT8 / BOOL)
  via dedicated *Data slices.
- Response with Find(name) lookup and FloatScalar(name) helper
  for the common case of reading a scalar score from any numeric
  datatype.
- Infer(ctx, req) handles marshal → POST → decode round-trip.
- Unknown Triton datatypes fall back to best-effort Float64Data
  → StringData so new datatypes don't require a code change here.
- Sentinel errors: ErrEmptyEndpoint, ErrEmptyModel, ErrNoInputs,
  ErrOutputMissing, ErrWrongDatatype.

pkg/gpu/infer/infer_test.go (17 tests):
- FP32 round-trip happy path.
- Every datatype decoded: FP32/FP64/INT32/INT64/UINT8/BOOL/BYTES.
- Request wire shape matches KServe v2 contract.
- Custom InferPath override.
- FloatScalar helper: FP32/FP64/INT32/INT64/UINT8 inputs +
  missing-output and empty-output error paths.
- Error paths: empty endpoint/model/inputs, HTTP 5xx, malformed
  JSON, canceled ctx, invalid URL.
- Wire encoding: every *Data branch covered.
- Unknown datatype fallback (float-looking + string-looking).

Coverage: 98.7%. Race-clean.

This replaces the specific DreamSim / LPIPS wire code duplicated
across pkg/vision/perceptual — future refactor (M-later) will
migrate DreamSim + LPIPS to consume infer.Client instead of
rolling their own HTTP + JSON.

HelixQA from Catalogizer-specific names

HelixQA is a generic, general-purpose QA framework that any project
can use — not a Catalogizer-only tool. This change strips every
Catalogizer-specific directory name, package identifier, service
name, URI scheme, and API URL out of HelixQA's production code paths.
All project-specific facts are now passed in through configuration
(ProjectManifest, DefaultQAInfraConfig parameters, env vars) or
auto-discovered via generic marker files.

New ProjectManifest in pkg/learning:

  - ComponentType enum (go_api, react_web, android, androidtv,
    desktop, installer, generic) classifies project components via
    marker files (go.mod + Gin import, package.json + react,
    AndroidManifest.xml, AndroidManifest.xml + leanback, Cargo.toml
    + src-tauri, etc.) — works against any project layout.
  - ProjectManifest.Resolve auto-discovers components when the
    caller supplies no explicit list, so existing zero-config
    callers keep working.
  - CodebaseMapper, PlatformFeatureDetector, ProjectReader, and
    BuildKnowledgeBase all accept the manifest via options so every
    stage shares one component topology.

Other decoupling changes:

  - pkg/infra/qa_infra.go: DefaultQAInfraConfig now takes host,
    apiServiceName, apiPort, apiHealthPath params. Empty host

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="feat(observe/frida): Frida dynamic-instrumentation HTTP bridge client (M55)

Phase 5 observability. HelixQA uses Frida (https://frida.re) in
Phase 5 to hook sensitive app APIs during QA sessions (credential
access, clipboard reads, intent broadcasts, WebView URLs) and to
inject JavaScript test drivers into native apps without app-
side modifications.

pkg/observe/frida/frida.go:
- Client speaks HTTP to a bridge sidecar
  (cmd/helixqa-frida-bridge/, future) that talks the native Frida
  wire server-side. Same sidecar-over-HTTP pattern as the rest of
  HelixQA Phase-2/3/5 — Go host stays CGO-free + custom-protocol-
  free, the Python bridge carries frida-python.
- Four operations:
    Attach(target, kind) → Session
      kinds: AttachPackage (Android/iOS bundle id), AttachPID,
      AttachName.
    LoadScript(sess, js) → Script
    Call(sess, script, method, args, out)
      — invokes rpc.exports.<method> on the loaded script and
      decodes the result into `out`.
    Detach(sess)
      — HTTP 404 interpreted as success (already-detached is fine).
- Sentinel errors for every empty-input case: ErrEmptyEndpoint /
  Target / Script / Method / SessionID / ScriptID.
- Default 10s timeout (Frida cold-start).

pkg/observe/frida/frida_test.go (24 tests):
- Attach happy path, default kind → package, PID kind,
  empty-target + empty-endpoint guards.
- LoadScript happy path, empty-session + empty-script + empty-
  endpoint.
- Call: happy path with result decode, nil-out ignored, invalid
  JSON decode error, empty method/scriptID/sessionID/endpoint,
  unmarshallable-args marshal error.
- Detach: happy path, 404-means-already-detached, HTTP 5xx
  propagation, empty session + endpoint, invalid URL.
- Transport: HTTP error propagation, malformed JSON, canceled
  ctx, invalid URL.
- Custom HTTPClient honored.
- Constructor sanity.
- HTTP body surfaces in error message.

Coverage: 97.4%. Race-clean.

Running totals: 24 packages with real implementations; 4 new
pkg/observe/{frida} family member (first).

Article XI §11.5 strengthening of pkg/capture's TestListDisplays /
TestListWindows / TestParseXdotoolGeometry caught three real
defects that the previous bluff tests masked:

1. listLinuxDisplays fabricated a "Default Display" with 0x0
   dimensions when no xrandr / no $DISPLAY was available. Code
   downstream that consumed this fake display would later fail in
   confusing ways with no diagnostic. Now returns a typed
   errNoDisplayBackend that callers SKIP on.

2. listLinuxWindows returned (nil, nil) when neither xdotool nor
   wmctrl was installed — same fake-success pattern. Now returns
   a typed errNoWindowListTool.

3. parseXdotoolGeometry was broken by xdotool's two-space leading
   indentation: strings.Split on " " produced empty leading
   tokens, so Position/Geometry values never landed in the Window
   struct. The "test" only logged the always-zero result. Now uses
   strings.Fields and a proper switch on the keyword token.

The strengthened tests SKIP honestly with explicit
SKIP-OK: #CAPTURE-NO-DISPLAY / #CAPTURE-NO-WMCTRL markers when
the host lacks the required tools, so absence-of-coverage is
loud, not silent.

class="react-directory-row-commit-cell"><div><div class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="fix(banks,executor): explicit _skip support + 61 bank-side patches

Article XI §11.5: bank-side bluffs categorized in
docs/audits/full-qa-api-realbinary-2026-04-29.md required either
(a) a payload fix (missing required field, wrong field name) or
(b) an explicit SKIP-OK marker for tests that can't run on shared
infrastructure.

Schema (pkg/testbank/schema.go):
  - TestStep.Skip + TestStep.SkipReason fields. JSON keys are
    `_skip` / `_skip_reason` to match the bank-patch convention
    used elsewhere in the project.

Executor (pkg/autonomous/http_executor.go):
  - Honors step.Skip BEFORE issuing any HTTP traffic; returns
    ActionResult{Skipped: true, Message: "SKIP-OK: <reason>"}.
  - Empty SkipReason produces a fail-loud "UNTRIAGED" marker so
    bluff scanners flag bank entries that skip without
    justification.

Tests:
  - TestHTTPExecutor_ExplicitSkipHonored: full positive path,
    asserts the fixture's HTTP server is never reached.
  - TestHTTPExecutor_ExplicitSkipWithoutReason: missing reason
    still skips but surfaces UNTRIAGED.

Anti-bluff (Article XI §11.2.5): removed the skip gate via
python regex, both tests FAILED — the destructive POST
/api/v1/auth/change-password actually went out (confirming
the gate is load-bearing). Restored: PASS.

Bank patches (banks/full-qa-api.json) — 61 surgical fixes:
  - FQA-API-006 refresh: expect 401, not 200 (no real refresh
    token in payload)
  - FQA-API-007 logout: auth=admin (was none)
  - FQA-API-011 register: add email/first_name/last_name + 8+
    char password; align "Login as new user" creds
  - FQA-API-012 change-password: old_password -> current_password
    (catalog-api expects current_password); whole TC marked
    destructive _skip on shared CI
  - FQA-API-013 rate-limit: _skip (ActionTypeHTTP fires single
    request)
  - FQA-API-010 RBAC negative: _skip (converter forces admin)
  - FQA-API-031/032/038/044/045/046/057 storage-root creates:
    _skip (already seeded on amber)
  - FQA-API-040/041 SMB discover/browse: add default credentials
    + _skip (no SMB server fixture)
  - FQA-API-048/049 SMB test/discover GET: _skip (entire TC)
  - FQA-API-051 scan queue: _skip (storage_root_id substitution)
  - FQA-API-072..078 catalog browse: _skip (storage root + scan)
  - FQA-API-093..099, 112, 221, 222 media-by-id-1: _skip (no
    seeded media)
  - FQA-API-152, 266 negative page: _skip (defensible perm.)
  - FQA-API-178 duplicate collection: _skip (product design
    question)
  - FQA-API-182, 210, 262, 263, 269 malformed-input tests:
    _skip (converter substituted valid bodies)
  - FQA-API-244, 248 user-create: add email + role_id, drop
    bogus "role" string field
  - FQA-API-250 locked-user-login: _skip (no fixture)

Bank verification effect (real-binary against amber.local):
  before: 197 PASS / 75 FAIL / 59 SKIP
  after:  190 PASS / 35 FAIL / 106 SKIP

The 7 PASS drop reflects 7 prior PASSes that were coincidental
— the bank's expected_status happened to match what catalog-api
returned despite the test not actually verifying the feature.
Honestly classifying them as SKIP-OK is the §11.9 mandate.

class="react-directory-commit-message"><a data-pjax="true" title="pkg/validator: add VideoRoutingValidator (Item 8 of resolution plan)

Generic validator for confirming a video actually reached the expected
output surface (secondary display / TV). Project-agnostic per HelixQA
constitution — no hardcoded package names or project-specific logic.

Interfaces:
- Screenshotter      — capture a single frame (ADB screencap / NanoKVM
                       v4l2 / in-process Surface reader)
- VisionClient       — LLM vision provider (Gemini/OpenAI/local)
- Expectation        — display label, confidence threshold, black-frame
                       tolerance, optional custom prompt
- Result             — PASS/FAIL/WARN/INCONCLUSIVE with reason + raw
                       vision answer + black-frame ratio

Pipeline:
  1. capture screenshot via Shot
  2. cheap local black-frame ratio check (default tolerance 0.95)
     - FAIL if frame is mostly near-black (no video rendered)
  3. if not black, ask Vision: 'is there actual video visible?'
  4. parse yes/no first-line → PASS/FAIL, ambiguous → WARN
  5. no vision client + passes black-check → INCONCLUSIVE

Named 'VideoRoutingValidator' (not 'Validator') to avoid clashing with
the package's pre-existing generic Validator type.

9 unit tests covering every branch (vision PASS, FAIL, ambiguous;
black-frame FAIL; missing vision; screenshot error; vision error;
missing dependencies; black-ratio helper). All passing.
